newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE'S Vranitzky to urge foreign help in Albania.
newsitem.headline: OSCE'S Vranitzky to urge foreign help in Albania.

text.p: European mediator Franz Vranitzky said on Friday he would urge the European Union and OSCE member states to give serious thought to a request from Tirana to send in military support to Albania.

Vranitzky, speaking to Reuters in Vienna by telephone from the Italian frigate Aliseo in the Adriatic where he was holding talks with Albanian government leaders, said he believed order could only be restored in Albania with outside help.
"I think order can only be established with help from abroad," the former Austrian chancellor said.
He said he was told by Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, Foreign Minister Arjan Starova and army chief of staff General Adem Copani that they could not cope with the situation by themselves.
"They believe they can overcome it if there is support from abroad," Vranitzky added.

Vranitzky said he would speak as soon as possible to Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo of the Netherlands, whose country currently holds the EU presidency, and Denmark's foreign minister, Niels Helveg Petersen, current chairman of the 54-member state Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
"I will urge them today, or at the latest tomorrow, to make a decision one way or the other," he said.

"I think the OSCE and the EU countries should give it very thorough thought because this seems to be the most urgent answer the Albanians have to get, otherwise chaos and anarchy will continue," he added.

Vranitzky said it should be made clear that the request for military or police assistance in Albania would be made to individual governments and not to any particular body such as the Western European Union, considered the EU's future defence arm.
He said the request to individual governments should be made by the Netherland's Van Mierlo or Denmark's Petersen.
